epic.name: Hazine Hardening and Delivery
decisions: The controller must verify epic-hazine-experience completed and its full experience gates passed before launching this epic.
Spectrum runs in the canonical repository created by Phase 0; no working-copy-to-canonical sync occurs here.
Original GLBs and approved brand assets remain immutable; only optimized derivatives are promoted.
One live motion policy governs all animation engines and CSS.
Deployment is commit-based from the canonical repository and rollback redeploys the last known-good commit.
outOfScope: Production integrations, business KPIs, production latency, and unvalidated starter extraction
risks: Incomplete motion shutdown across multiple engines
Attribution loss during optimization
Working/canonical repository divergence
Pages subpath regressions
Premature publication of an unverified commit

stories.title: Show authored loading states
stories.description: As a visitor, I see intentional route, lazy scene-module, and asset-loading states while Hazine prepares.

steps.description: Define distinct route, module, and asset loading states.
Expose visible progress where measurable.
Simulate each loading state and verify authored presentation.

context.why: Loading is part of the product margin, not a blank gap.
risks: Nested suspense states can obscure one another.
edgeCases: Cached instant loads and stalled assets.
patterns: Use SceneAssetGroup and route-level suspense boundaries.

stories.title: Contain scene and module failures
stories.description: As a visitor, lazy-module, WebGL, scene, and asset failures are caught by an explicit boundary with a retry path.

steps.description: Create an error boundary that classifies supported failure modes.
Add bounded retry/reset behavior.
Inject each failure and verify no uncaught error escapes.

context.why: A shareable experience must fail intentionally.
risks: Retry loops can repeatedly crash.
edgeCases: Context loss and failure during retry.
patterns: Contain the Canvas and lazy modules at stable boundaries.

stories.title: Provide a WebGL-free experience
stories.description: As a visitor without usable WebGL, I receive an intentional static narrative experience instead of a broken canvas.

steps.description: Detect WebGL availability before scene startup.
Render chapter-appropriate static visuals and working product UI.
Verify all essential meaning remains accessible without Canvas.

context.why: 3D is narrative infrastructure, but access to the story cannot depend on GPU support.
risks: Fallback can become an empty poster.
edgeCases: Context loss after a WebGL crash.
patterns: StaticSceneFallback preserves DOM interaction and chapter state.

stories.title: Apply live motion preference globally
stories.description: As a user, live prefers-reduced-motion changes immediately govern GSAP, Anime.js, R3F actors, seal, globe, camera, pointer effects, and CSS.

steps.description: Create a subscribed central motion policy.
Route every engine and CSS state through it.
Toggle preference live in every chapter and surface.

context.why: A page-load-only check leaves active motion running after preference changes.
risks: One engine can bypass the shared switch.
edgeCases: Change preference mid-timeline or mid-camera passage.
patterns: Centralize policy and cancel active timelines before applying static states.

stories.title: Remove all decorative reduced-motion movement
stories.description: As a reduced-motion user, no decorative spatial or CSS motion remains active while state changes retain clear meaning.

steps.description: Inventory seal, globe, actor, pointer, Sparkles, camera, GSAP, Anime.js, and CSS motion.
Replace decorative transitions with immediate/static meaningful states.
Record zero-motion verification evidence.

context.why: Reduced motion is a release criterion, not a partial aesthetic setting.
risks: Shader/time uniforms or CSS pseudo-elements remain active.
edgeCases: Hover and focus feedback must remain visible without motion.
patterns: Use the shared useMotionPolicy result everywhere.

stories.title: Preserve original and approved assets
stories.description: As a maintainer, source GLBs under assets/original and approved public/brand assets remain byte-for-byte untouched while derivatives are produced elsewhere.

steps.description: Record immutable source paths and checksums in the manifest.
Make inspection fail if a source/approved asset changes.
Verify processing writes only derivatives.

context.why: Original client assets and approved identity cannot be silently rewritten.
risks: In-place tools can destroy recoverable source quality.
edgeCases: Same filename across original and public directories.
patterns: Manifest is the single asset pipeline source of truth.

stories.title: Drive asset tools from one manifest
stories.description: As a maintainer, inspect, repair, optimize, validate, promote, and gltfjsx generation all consume one asset manifest.

steps.description: Define source, repair hook, optimization, validation, promotion, generation, and license fields.
Remove hard-coded per-script asset lists.
Run every tool over the same manifest records.

context.why: A repeatable pipeline cannot depend on diverging script inventories.
risks: Schema drift can break all tooling at once.
edgeCases: Assets that intentionally skip repair or generation.
patterns: Follow scripts/inspect-assets.mjs:18-65 and optimize-assets.mjs:5-37.

stories.title: Validate derivatives and retain attribution
stories.description: As a maintainer or visitor, every optimized GLB is validated and its source/license attribution remains recorded and publishable.

steps.description: Run structural validation after optimization.
Fail promotion for invalid output or missing license metadata.
Generate or update visible attribution documentation.

context.why: Optimization must not sever provenance or ship broken geometry.
risks: CC BY attribution can be lost between stages.
edgeCases: Multiple authors/licenses per asset.
patterns: Keep license metadata on each manifest record.

stories.title: Promote assets through an explicit pipeline
stories.description: As a maintainer, optimized artifacts reach public/models and generated components only through a repeatable validate-then-promote step.

steps.description: Implement explicit repair, optimize, validate, promote, and generate stages.
Expose repeatable package scripts without implicit in-place writes.
Run the full pipeline twice and compare outputs.

context.why: Public assets must be reproducible from preserved originals.
risks: Partial promotion can mix old and new derivatives.
edgeCases: Failure after validation but before generation.
patterns: Promote only validated outputs, then run gltfjsx.

stories.title: Keep render loops allocation-free
stories.description: As a visitor, custom frame loops avoid per-frame object allocation and React state writes that degrade interaction.

steps.description: Audit every custom useFrame callback.
Memoize/reuse vectors, scalars, and traversal buffers.
Replace frame-driven React state with imperative refs.

context.why: Allocation churn undermines smooth cinematic transitions.
risks: High-blast-radius director changes affect every actor.
edgeCases: Responsive profile changes outside frame loops.
patterns: Keep imperative delta-time updates; remove new Vector3() in useFrame.

stories.title: Dispose cloned materials safely
stories.description: As a visitor navigating or retrying scenes, cloned materials are released exactly once without disposing shared source materials.

steps.description: Track ownership for cloned versus shared materials.
Dispose owned clones on actor/group unmount.
Exercise mount, retry, and unmount cycles for leaks/double disposal.

context.why: Scene retries and lazy groups must not leak GPU resources.
risks: Disposing shared materials corrupts other actors.
edgeCases: Multiple meshes sharing one clone.
patterns: Centralize ownership in materialLifecycle.js.

stories.title: Support complex material shapes
stories.description: As a viewer, actor fading preserves material arrays and transparent/glass behavior instead of assuming one opaque material.

steps.description: Normalize single and array material traversal.
Preserve transparency, depth, and glass-specific properties while fading.
Verify representative opaque, transparent, glass, and array actors.

context.why: Global material mutation currently affects every GLB unsafely.
risks: Generic opacity changes can break glass rendering.
edgeCases: Null entries and nested material arrays.
patterns: Refactor HazineScene.jsx:44-102 through materialLifecycle.

stories.title: Lazy-load chapter scene groups
stories.description: As a visitor, narrative actors load by chapter-oriented group rather than all blocking the initial scene.

steps.description: Assign GLBs to manifest preload groups.
Load current and bounded next groups lazily.
Verify group failure remains contained and retryable.

context.why: Late narrative assets must not delay threshold interaction.
risks: Too-late preloading causes visible scene gaps.
edgeCases: Fast jumps to a distant chapter.
patterns: Use chapter-oriented SceneAssetGroup boundaries.

stories.title: Measure before reducing scene fidelity
stories.description: As a maintainer, I receive bundle, transferred-byte, and frame-time baselines before any further mesh or shader reduction.

steps.description: Measure bundle composition and transferred assets.
Measure median frame time across defined transitions and profiles.
Record baselines before deciding any fidelity reduction.

context.why: Optimization without evidence can damage the experience without helping users.
risks: Non-repeatable capture conditions invalidate comparisons.
edgeCases: Warm cache versus cold load.
patterns: Measure first; preserve authored quality until a measured bottleneck exists.

stories.title: Keep threshold usable during late loads
stories.description: As a visitor, I can interact with the first chapter and its static scene while later 3D groups continue loading.

steps.description: Separate first-interaction readiness from late-group completion.
Show the authored static scene until each group is ready.
Throttle late groups and verify the threshold remains operable.

context.why: Heavy 3D must not block the product's entry point.
risks: A global loading overlay can still capture interaction.
edgeCases: Late group fails permanently.
patterns: Progressive scene groups plus StaticSceneFallback.

stories.title: Apply editorial and semantic visual restraint
stories.description: As a viewer, large copy stays restrained, labels stay concise, approved assets are used unchanged, gold means attention/value, mineral green means living context, and anomaly/danger colors remain reserved.

steps.description: Audit visible copy and operational labels.
Audit semantic color use across story, plugin, and workbench.
Compare rendered identity assets to approved public/brand sources.

context.why: Visual language communicates epistemic role and attention.
risks: Overusing gold or green erases meaning.
edgeCases: Warning-like confidence states that are not danger.
patterns: Use the locked ivory/dark-rail palette and immutable assets.

stories.title: Honor motion hierarchy and timing budgets
stories.description: As a viewer, motion follows leader/follower sequencing with 20-40% overlap, feedback begins within 150ms, UI transitions land within 350ms, and cinematic transitions remain within 600-1500ms.

steps.description: Encode timing and overlap budgets by beat type.
Apply budgets to UI, DOM lines, actors, and camera.
Measure representative interactions and transitions.

context.why: Authored timing lets the interface yield and return deliberately.
risks: Engine-specific easing can extend perceived duration.
edgeCases: Interrupted and reduced-motion transitions.
patterns: One leader, followers overlap 20-40%; Anime.js for DOM, R3F/Theatre for 3D.

stories.title: Pass interaction accessibility checks
stories.description: As a keyboard or low-vision user, every control has semantics, labels, visible focus, and readable contrast even over dark or luminous 3D apertures.

steps.description: Audit semantic roles and accessible names.
Keyboard every interactive path and repair focus behavior.
Measure contrast across transparent scene backgrounds and both target viewports.

context.why: The margins are product and zero accessibility blockers is a success measure.
risks: Dynamic backgrounds can invalidate static contrast checks.
edgeCases: Focus after surface switch, retry, and chapter jump.
patterns: Use visible non-color-only focus and opaque contrast protection where needed.

stories.title: Verify responsive live-intelligence phases
stories.description: As a reviewer, every live-intelligence phase passes visual checks at 1440x900 and 390x844.

steps.description: Enumerate all live-intelligence phases and states.
Capture both required viewports for each state.
Record pass/fail evidence and resolve every failure before exit.

context.why: Fixed viewport evidence catches responsive 3D/UI competition.
risks: Sampling only chapter defaults misses selected states.
edgeCases: Loading, failure, and reduced-motion variants.
patterns: Include all transcript selections and both surfaces.

stories.title: Eliminate runtime and dependency errors
stories.description: As a visitor or reviewer, the verified flows have no uncaught or unexpected console errors and the obsolete r3f-globe wrapper is absent.

steps.description: Assert package and lockfile contain no r3f-globe.
Run root/workbench desktop/mobile flows with console capture.
Remove unexpected errors and document only unavoidable warnings.

context.why: Clean runtime evidence is required before extraction.
risks: Warnings can conceal real errors.
edgeCases: Errors appearing only on direct route or retry.
patterns: Keep direct three-globe and record console evidence.

stories.title: Meet measured performance gates
stories.description: As a visitor, hardening does not regress initial transferred bytes or median frame time by more than 10%, and active 3D transitions sustain at least 30 FPS on the defined low-power profile.

steps.description: Repeat baseline measurements under identical conditions.
Compare bytes and median frame time to STORY-056.
Verify 30 FPS floor and remediate measured regressions only.

context.why: Performance quality needs a measurable floor without premature fidelity loss.
risks: Hardware/noise differences can produce false regressions.
edgeCases: Cold-load versus active-transition profiles.
patterns: Use the recorded baseline and defined low-power fixture.

stories.title: Reproduce the production build
stories.description: As a maintainer, a clean frozen dependency install reproducibly builds the root and Pages-compatible workbench artifacts from the canonical source tree.

steps.description: Install from the frozen lockfile in a clean environment.
Build and assert root, workbench, 404, and base-prefixed artifacts.
Make the Pages workflow execute the same build path.

context.why: Delivery must be reproducible from the canonical repository.
risks: Local caches can hide undeclared inputs.
edgeCases: Repository name/base differs from local /hazine/ simulation.
patterns: Single build script shared by local verification and CI.

stories.title: Record complete Hazine acceptance evidence
stories.description: As a reviewer, every PRD acceptance criterion and phase quality gate has concrete pass/fail evidence in one validation report.

steps.description: Map every Hazine acceptance criterion to commands, captures, and observed results.
Include responsive, motion, failure, provenance, console, asset, and performance evidence.
Leave no criterion without a resolved pass or explicit failure.

context.why: Starter extraction requires proof, not confidence.
risks: A report can claim checks without preserving evidence.
edgeCases: Provisional performance gates must state fixture conditions.
patterns: Use one acceptance-to-evidence matrix.

stories.title: Review the final canonical diff
stories.description: As a maintainer, the final canonical diff contains only intended Hazine and validation changes while preserving Phase 0 history, unmatched user files, and unrelated work.

steps.description: Compare the final branch to the recorded Phase 0 baseline commit.
Review every changed path and record the intended story or validation source.
Confirm .git history, unmatched user files, and unrelated work remain intact.

context.why: Final delivery must remain traceable to the reviewed baseline without a second risky filesystem sync.
risks: Unrelated canonical edits can be swept into the release commit.
edgeCases: User changes made after Phase 0 and generated artifacts that should not ship.
patterns: Review from the recorded baseline commit; do not copy or mirror the non-Git workspace again.

stories.title: Deploy only the verified commit
stories.description: As a maintainer, the reviewed final canonical state is committed atomically and that exact commit is deployed through the remote and Pages target already proven by the preview.

steps.description: Commit the reviewed final canonical diff atomically.
Reconfirm the configured remote, deployment branch, and Pages source match the preview proof.
Push the final commit and observe the Pages workflow for the same SHA.

context.why: Publishing must never outrun review or target discovery.
risks: A changed remote, branch, or workflow can deploy a different commit.
edgeCases: No remote exists or Pages is not yet configured.
patterns: Reuse the preview-proven target; commit-based deployment with SHA equality.

stories.title: Validate the public Hazine proof
stories.description: As a reviewer, the public root, chapter anchor, and direct /workbench URL load the verified commit with assets, interactions, console, and mobile layout passing, and the canonical repository is clean at that deployed SHA.

steps.description: Confirm remote main and Pages deployment resolve to the reviewed commit.
Exercise public root, anchor, and workbench on desktop/mobile with console capture.
Record live URLs, commit SHA, evidence, and clean canonical status.

context.why: This is the proof boundary that permits starter extraction.
risks: CI success can mask CDN, path, or runtime failures.
edgeCases: Cached older deploy and direct-route 404 behavior.
patterns: Verify the public artifact, not only the workflow result.
